account:
Today I kept my morning office appointment; the secretary reports no new correspondence. I am now at the mill, early for my ten o'clock grain inspection. Later I have lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea with my neighbour at fifteen, and office at sixteen thirty.

The unusual business is the great hall preparation: lanterns have been placed, and yesterday I personally saw both builder and innkeeper deposit bread in the eastern table chest. My neighbour says freight described the delivery as paid catering. The neighbour also reports seeing innkeeper pay the baker and hearing an offer of two hundred fresh loaves for 104 emeralds plus builder's materials. I did not witness that transaction myself.

The secretary has now heard from innkeeper and freight that this is an evening community hospitality gathering, with its programme to be announced at eighteen today. Innkeeper personally invited me, said local helpers are arranging it together, and offered to collect me from my office shortly beforehand. I accepted, and the secretary confirmed the reservation. Innkeeper says I should simply attend as a guest, with no remarks prepared.

This appears to explain the bread and lighting, though the precise programme and original commissioner remain unknown to me. The quantity of bread suggests substantial hospitality. I suspect the organisers want to keep some details until the announcement, but I have no evidence of a hidden purpose beyond the gathering they described.
